title: Two injured in Kollupitiya shooting
byline: A shooting was reported at a housing complex located on 6th Lane in Kollupitiya in the early hours of today (04), Police said.

title: Transplanted pig kidney works in US man’s body for record 271 days
byline: A kidney transplanted from a pig has worked inside a patient for 271 days – the longest on record, say US doctors.

title: Johnston Fernando appears before Bribery Commission
byline: Former Minister Johnston Fernando appeared before the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) today.

title: Crop damage compensation payments begin today
byline: The payment of compensation to farmers for crops damaged due to adverse weather conditions in several districts will commence today (04), the Agriculture and Farmers’ Insurance Board said.

title: CPC reduces prices of furnace oil and naphtha
byline: The Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC) has decided to reduce the prices of furnace oil and naphtha, with the new prices coming into effect from midnight today (04).

title: Namal arrives at Bribery Commission
byline: SLPP National Organiser and Parliamentarian Namal Rajapaksa arrived at the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) this morning to provide a statement regarding the Airbus deal.

title: Police do not send SMS or WhatsApp links for fine payments: Traffic DIG
byline: Sri Lanka Police have warned the public about a fraudulent WhatsApp and SMS scam circulating under the guise of the Colombo Traffic Police, demanding online payments for alleged traffic violations.

title: Police turn to professional designers for new uniform
byline: Sri Lanka Police to work with professional fashion designers to create a new modern uniform as part of efforts to upgrade and modernize the police service, President Anura Kumara Dissanayake said.

title: IMF team to visit Sri Lanka for key economic review in September
byline: An International Monetary Fund (IMF) staff team is scheduled to visit Sri Lanka from September 10 to 23, 2026, for discussions with government authorities as the country prepares for another key assessment of its ongoing economic reform program.

title: Man arrested for circulating ex-wife’s nude photographs on social media
byline: A 36-year-old man has been arrested in connection with the alleged circulation of nude photographs of a woman on social media, police said.

title: Namal Rajapaksa to appear before Bribery Commission today
byline: MP Namal Rajapaksa is scheduled to appear before the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) today.

title: Dudley Sirisena spends Rs. 35 mn to renovate Polonnaruwa Railway Station
byline: Sri Lankan businessman Dudley Sirisena said he had spent Rs. 35 million to renovate the Polonnaruwa Railway Station and pledged to maintain the station at his own expense for one year.

title: Bribery Commission reveals charges against Johnston
byline: Former Minister of Co-operatives and Internal Trade Johnston Fernando and Design Point (Pvt) Ltd. owner Patabendigige Hemantha Lalith de Silva were arrested this morning by officers of the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) over an alleged corruption case involving the procurement of chairs for the Mahinda Rajapaksa Theatre in Polgolla.

title: Labour Ministry clarifies Sri Lanka’s national minimum wage ranking
byline: The Labour Ministry has clarified that a recent international comparison ranking Sri Lanka 120th globally in terms of its national minimum wage was based on 2024 data published by Visual Capitalist and was not an International Labour Organization (ILO) report.

title: Police step up school drug searches; IGP calls on schools to seek police assistance
byline: Steps are underway to conduct searches for narcotics in schools across the country, with IGP Priyantha Weerasuriya calling on schools to seek police assistance, including sniffer dogs and officers, in the fight against drugs among schoolchildren.

title: Two trapped tunnel workers rescued 9 days after floods hit Nepal
byline: Two hydropower workers were pulled from a tunnel buried by debris in Nepal on Friday, more than a week after catastrophic flooding swept through the area, government ministers said.

title: Royal College Archers Shine at Wayamba Youth and Junior Archery Championship, 2026
byline: Royal College produced a strong overall performance at the Wayamba Youth and Junior Archery Championship 2026, securing third place in the team standings with a total of 72 points. The achievement reflected the growing strength and depth of archery at Royal, with the young Archers recording notable results across several age categories.

title: Dengue cases fall, but Sri Lanka not out of the woods
byline: Although the number of dengue cases has declined significantly, the risk of the disease remains, with health authorities urging the public to continue taking precautions against mosquito breeding.

title: Sun directly overhead over six areas today
byline: The Sun will be directly overhead at around 12:09 p.m. today (4) over Nittambuwa, Algama, Malwana, Aranayake, Meegahakivula and Panadura, the Meteorology Department said.

title: Asalanka to lead Sri Lanka for England T20Is as Mendis sits out
byline: Sri Lanka will be without Kusal Mendis and Binura Fernando for the upcoming T20I series against England, as both players continue rehabilitation following injuries sustained during the Lanka Premier League 2026.

title: Namal ready for independent investigations, says political future rests with people
byline: Former Parliamentarian Namal Rajapaksa said he was prepared to face independent investigations at any time, while expressing concern that political statements made in Parliament were creating doubts about the independence of the police and judiciary.

title: Legal fraternity voices concern as experienced judge retires without elevation to SC
byline: Court of Appeal Justice Rathanapriya Gurusinghe retired on September 1, prompting renewed concerns within the legal community over the failure to elevate an experienced career judge to the Supreme Court despite the existence of four vacancies.

title: U.S. maritime chiefs to visit Sri Lanka
byline: U.S. Federal Maritime Commission (FMC) Chairman Laura DiBella and FMC Commissioner Robert J. Harvey will visit Sri Lanka September 6–10 to advance U.S.-Sri Lanka cooperation on maritime trade, investment, and the shipping networks connecting American businesses and consumers to markets across the Indo-Pacific. During her visit, Chairman DiBella and Commissioner Harvey will meet with senior Sri Lankan government and maritime leaders.

title: Johnston Fernando arrested
byline: Former Minister Johnston Fernando has been arrested by the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) in connection with an ongoing investigation.

title: ’’Never asked mahout to produce elephant before police’’ - DIG
byline: Police never instructed a mahout to bring his elephant after a dagger-like weapon was found in his possession during a road search conducted amid this year’s Kandy Esala Perahera, Central Province Deputy Inspector General of Police Sudath Masinghe said.

title: CEJ installs awareness boards in Anuradhapura to promote human-elephant coexistence
byline: The Center for Environmental Justice (CEJ) has taken steps to install awareness boards in several key ecological areas in Anuradhapura to promote human-elephant coexistence and protect the country’s natural heritage.

title: Sri Lanka, Bhutan discuss closer cooperation in education
byline: Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya held bilateral talks with Bhutanese Minister for Education and Skills Development Yeezang De Thapa on September 3, focusing on strengthening cooperation between Sri Lanka and Bhutan in education and vocational training.

title: Rs. 250 mn cancer drugs at risk of being destroyed
byline: A stock of cancer medicine worth more than Rs. 250 million is at risk of being destroyed due to a dispute over its regulatory approval, while cancer patients are already facing shortages of essential medicines, Doctors’ Trade Union Alliance for Medical and Civil Rights Chairman Specialist Dr. Chamal Sanjeewa said.

title: Senior parliament staff summoned to CIABOC
byline: Several senior Parliament officials have given statements to the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) in connection with a complaint filed against Speaker Jagath Wickramaratne by former Secretary General of Parliament Chaminda Kularatne.

title: British army told to stop non-essential training exercises to save money
byline: The Army has been told to stop ’’non-essential’’ training exercises to save money, according to a defence source.

title: First coal shipment arrives in Puttalam for Norochcholai power plant
byline: The first coal shipment for the Norochcholai Lakvijaya Power Plant in the second quarter of this year has arrived at Puttalam, with unloading expected to commence this afternoon, authorities said.

title: Metro Bus aims to establish new public transport culture: Presidential Secretary
byline: Presidential Secretary Dr. Nandika Sanath Kumanayake said the main objective of the Metro Bus service was to establish a new culture in public transportation by providing passengers with a more comfortable, safe and respectful travel experience.

title: Bribery Commission arrests Namal after five-hour questioning
byline: Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) National Organiser and Parliamentarian Namal Rajapaksa was arrested by the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) following more than five hours of questioning today over the Airbus deal.

title: SC concludes hearing into Anti-Corruption (Amendment) Bill
byline: The Supreme Court today concluded hearing arguments for and against the constitutionality of the proposed Anti-Corruption (Amendment) Bill.

title: Sri Lanka may experience hotter, drier conditions in early 2027 amid El Niño
byline: Sri Lanka may experience changes in rainfall patterns and rising temperatures in the coming months as El Niño conditions develop, Meteorology Department Director General  Ajith Wijemanna said.

title: Suspected remains of missing Fast Attack Craft officer recovered
byline: The Sri Lanka Navy has recovered remains suspected to be those of the officer who went missing following the maritime incident involving Fast Attack Craft P 4447 on August 15.

title: Two drowned after boat capsizes in Kattankudy
byline: Two people have reportedly drowned while another person was rescued after a boat capsized in a tank in Kattankudy, Batticaloa.

title: Defence challenges credibility of Nimal Perera in Namal Rajapaksa Airbus case
byline: President’s Counsel Sampath Mendis, appearing on behalf of suspect Namal Rajapaksa, told the Colombo Chief Magistrate’s Court that his client had been arrested and produced before court solely on the basis of a statement by businessman Nimal Perera.

title: Arrests will not deter public acceptance of politicians: UNP
byline: While condemning the arrest of SLPP MP Namal Rajapaksa, the United National Party (UNP) today said that public acceptance of a politician will not be deterred by arrests.

title: Muzammil’s son Jamaldeen arrested over alleged fraud
byline: Mohamed Hisham Jamaldeen, the son of former Western Province Governor and former Colombo Mayor A.J.M. Muzammil was arrested at the Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA) on Wednesday (September 2).

title: Water supply to be suspended in parts of Colombo, Battaramulla
byline: The National Water Supply and Drainage Board (NWSDB) has announced that the water supply will be suspended until 11.30 p.m. on September 5, 2026, due to maintenance work being carried out on the Ambatale–Dehiwala water transmission pipeline near Diyatha Uyana in Battaramulla.

title: US diesel prices hit an all-time-high
byline: Drivers in the US are paying more than ever for diesel at the pump as the US-Israel war with Iran continues to hit Americans’ wallets.

title: CSE surges as broad-based buying pushes ASPI above 21,600
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange extended its positive momentum for a third consecutive session on Friday, 4 September 2026, with both benchmark indices recording gains of more than 1% amid a sharp improvement in buying interest across the broader market.

title: Johnston Fernando granted bail
byline: Former Minister Johnston Fernando and Design Point (Pvt) Ltd owner Hemantha Lalith de Silva were released on bail by Colombo Chief Magistrate Asanga S. Bodaragama over allegations of corruption in connection with the purchase of chairs for the Polgolla Mahinda Rajapaksa Auditorium.

title: Namal Rajapaksa remanded
byline: Parliamentarian Namal Rajapaksa, who was arrested by the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) over allegations of accepting a Rs. 100 million bribe in connection with a transaction involving the purchase of Airbus aircraft, has been ordered to be remanded until September 18 by Colombo Chief Magistrate Asanga S. Bodaragama today.

title: Why was Namal Rajapaksa arrested?
byline: MP Namal Rajapaksa has been arrested by officers of the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) over an alleged Rs. 100 million bribery case linked to transactions involving the purchase of aircraft for SriLankan Airlines.

title: US diesel prices hit an all-time-high
byline: Drivers in the US are paying more than ever for diesel at the pump as the US-Israel war with Iran continues to hit Americans’ wallets.
